rounds.text: Onemi Technology Solutions demonstrates massive scale and accelerating expansion, evidenced by AUM surging 68.4% YoY to Rs 9,317 Cr [E78], TTM profit growing 75% [E19] (net profit +102% YoY [E59]), and management raising its FY27 AUM growth guidance from 40% plus to 60% plus [E67]. Operational quality is reflected in a 30% TTM operating margin [E23], an ROE of 24.0% [E13], and an ROA of 7.64% [E8], both substantially higher than sector benchmarks of 5.57% [E9] and 1.89% [E8] respectively. Despite this growth, valuation remains modest at a P/E of 17.6x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 9.85x against the sector benchmark of 13.08x [E11], yielding a 56.7% margin of safety against a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 754 per share [E38, E39]. Institutional investors are accumulating shares, driven by a combined 9.34 percentage point increase in foreign and domestic holdings [E35, E36, E37], while total borrowings fell from Rs 2,429 Cr to Rs 1,643 Cr [E32] and borrowing costs dropped by roughly 70 basis points [E75]. Conceded: operating cash flow for Mar 2026 was negative at Rs -461 Cr with cash conversion at -1.64x [E27, E28], and promoter holding decreased to 20.42% [E34, E53, E54]. Nonetheless, propelled by sector macro tailwinds [E61, E63] and a rules-based screen score of 92 out of 100 [E56], the business is significantly under-appreciated given its expanding network of 12.8 million customers [E79].

Despite impressive reported profit growth and expanding AUM, Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd (KISSHT) exhibits severe cash generation failures that undermine the reliability of its reported earnings [E27, E28, E29]. Specifically, operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 461 crore and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 471 crore in March 2026, yielding an alarming cash conversion ratio of -1.64x against reported profit [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, insider confidence is eroding as promoter holdings decreased by 4.38 percentage points last quarter to a low base of 20.42% [E34, E54], and the stock price currently trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. The company also continues to distribute zero dividends despite reporting profits [E4, E52], while managing high borrowing costs that official commentary admits remain a drag [E55, E75]. Conceded: the company displays strong short-term sales growth, an institutional money inflow of +9.34 percentage points, and management guidance projecting robust AUM expansion for FY27 [E16, E37, E67]. However, high annualised volatility of 55.2% and an inconsistent operating margin trend over the last two quarters expose investors to significant downside variance [E26, E46].

Conceded: operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative Rs 461 crore and free cash flow was negative Rs 471 crore [E28, E29]. However, this cash burn must be contextualized against explosive top-line and balance-sheet expansion, with AUM surging 68.4% year-on-year to reach Rs 9,317 crore [E78], alongside management raising its FY27 AUM growth guidance to over 60% [E67] and completing a substantial Rs 832 crore preferential allotment to fund this scaling [E81, E83]. While promoter holding decreased to 20.42% [E34], this is overwhelmingly offset by massive institutional accumulation, with domestic and foreign institutions expanding their combined holdings by +9.34 percentage points [E37] and domestic institutions alone increasing their stake to 24.96% [E36]. Conceded: the stock trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43], yet relative strength stands at a robust 93 against the Nifty 500 [E44] and the Sharpe ratio sits at a strong 1.89 [E47]. The lack of dividend payout [E4] is standard for a high-growth compounding lender aggressively reinvesting capital into a financial services sector riding a strong macro tailwind of +0.78 [E63], while borrowing costs are actively falling, evidenced by the average cost of borrowing dropping from 14.45% to 13.76% and expected further reductions [E75, E76].

Conceded: AUM surged 68.4% year-on-year to reach Rs 9,317 crore and management raised its FY27 AUM growth guidance to over 60% [E67, E78]. However, this hyper-aggressive scaling is entirely disconnected from cash generation, evidenced by a devastating operating cash flow of Rs -461 crore and free cash flow of Rs -471 crore for March 2026 [E28, E29], resulting in a severe cash conversion ratio of -1.64x [E27]. Conceded: the preferential allotment brought in Rs 832 crore [E81, E83], but insiders are simultaneously fleeing the register as promoter holding plummeted by 4.38 percentage points last quarter to a paltry 20.42% [E34], an insider retreat explicitly flagged as a negative by filed statements [E53, E54]. Conceded: relative strength sits at 93 [E44] and institutional accumulation rose [E37], but technical momentum remains broken with the price sitting below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a punishing annualised volatility of 55.2% [E43, E46].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -461 Cr [E28], free cash flow stood at Rs -471 Cr [E29], and cash conversion was -1.64x in March 2026 [E27], but in a high-growth lending business expanding AUM by 68.4% YoY to Rs 9,317 Cr [E78], balance sheet funding is directly powered by robust net profit growth of 102% YoY [E59] alongside a fresh Rs 832.2 Cr preferential issue of which 75% is allocated to infuse capital into the subsidiary [E81, E82, E83]. This loan book expansion is accompanied by improving asset quality and efficiency, as credit cost dropped from 8.85% to 6.80% of average AUM [E77], management expects impairment costs to drop by over 15% YoY [E68], borrowings reduced from Rs 2,429 Cr to Rs 1,643 Cr [E32], and average cost of borrowing fell 70 basis points to 13.76% [E75]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased by 4.38 percentage points to 20.42% [E34, E53, E54], yet this shift was decisively absorbed by institutional buyers, resulting in overall positive institutional money flow [E37] with domestic institutional holding expanding by 5.91 percentage points to 24.96% [E36] and foreign institutional holding rising to 9.95% [E35]. Conceded: the price sits below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with annualised volatility of 55.2% [E43, E46], but underlying price strength remains firm with a relative-strength rating of 93 against the Nifty 500 [E44] and a strong Sharpe ratio of 1.89 [E47]. With a top-tier screen score of 92 out of 100 [E56] and an ROE of 24.0% [E13], the stock's current price of Rs 326 provides a 56.7% margin of safety against its DCF intrinsic value of Rs 754 per share [E2, E38, E39], while implying just 6.5% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case [E40].

Conceded: AUM grew 68.4% YoY to Rs 9,317 Cr [E78], and the company raised ₹832.2 Cr via a preferential issue [E83]. However, that massive growth has completely incinerated liquidity, resulting in a disastrous negative operating cash flow of Rs -461 Cr, a free cash flow of Rs -471 Cr, and a cash conversion ratio of -1.64x for March 2026 [E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: domestic and foreign institutions increased their stakes by a combined 8.22 percentage points [E35, E36], but this institutional accumulation occurred while promoters dumped 4.38 percentage points of their holding down to a meager 20.42% [E34]. Conceded: the relative strength rating is 93 against the Nifty 500 [E44] and the Sharpe ratio is 1.89 [E47], but the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages accompanied by a punishing 55.2% annualized volatility [E43, E46]. Furthermore, the bull's rosy valuation rests entirely on a speculative DCF intrinsic value of Rs 754 [E38], ignoring that the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], carries an inconsistent operating margin trend over the last two years and two quarters [E25, E26], and operates with a high borrowing cost [E55] that sits at a hefty 13.76% [E75].
